invariants: The producer side of hydra:autopilot:slot-events stays exactly as ADR-0017 sanctioned it (on-subagent-stop.sh's flat-field XADD via publishRaw() is untouched) — this concept is consumer-side only.

The new read is a PLAIN XREAD (not XREADGROUP): decide.py owns the cursor itself via state.slot_events_last_id, and this read must not create or advance a consumer-group position, so it cannot collide with the now-pixel bridge's independent 'now-pixel-bridge' group.

The endpoint is best-effort per the existing collect_slot_events contract: a Redis outage or empty stream must still yield the empty shape {"events": [], "last_id": null} with HTTP 200, never a 5xx that would abort the autopilot turn.

The new EventBus method is the ONLY place that re-derives {id, fields} from the raw XREAD reply — cascade-telemetry.ts and candidate-exclusions.ts's fromEvent() parsers keep consuming already-typed fields and are not touched.
collect_slot_events's emitted key (slot_events_json=<json>) and JSON shape stay byte-identical to today's output so decide.py's consumer needs zero changes.
No consumer-group state, WATCH, or MAXLEN write is introduced by this read path — it is read-only against the stream.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Route collect_slot_events through eventBus.consume() (the same XREADGROUP path slot-events-bridge.ts uses).
rejectedAlternatives.why: consume() is a durable-cursor consumer-group abstraction (ack, claim, recovery). decide.py's cursor is turn-local state in Redis-backed autopilot state (state.slot_events_last_id), not a consumer group identity — forcing it onto a group adds XACK/XAUTOCLAIM machinery the caller doesn't want and risks colliding with (or duplicating) the now-pixel bridge's own group semantics.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Fix the bash+regex parser in place (tighten the heuristic, add more test fixtures for the shell script).
rejectedAlternatives.why: Doesn't close the actual gap: the parser re-derives a wire format ioredis already returns structurally in a second language with zero test coverage under node:test. Hardening the regex still leaves a second, drift-prone implementation of the same format the TS side already owns correctly.

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Point collect_slot_events at redis-cli --no-raw plus jq (skip the Python regex, use RESP3/JSON-ish output).
rejectedAlternatives.why: redis-cli's XREAD output is not actually JSON in any mode — it is a formatted RESP dump. This still requires bespoke parsing of Redis wire semantics in bash/jq, just with a different heuristic; it doesn't route through the Event Bus seam ADR-0017 already designated as the owner of this format, and leaves scripts/ permanently outside redis-seam-check.ts's glob (the issue's own observation).

rejectedAlternatives.alt: Add a dedicated src/redis/slot-events-read.ts Category-A accessor instead of an EventBus method.
rejectedAlternatives.why: Streams are Category B under ADR-0017 ("the Event Bus owns stream ops; clients use its interface, never the raw connection") — a sibling redis/ file duplicating that ownership for one read method is exactly the shallow single-owner accessor ADR-0017 warns against creating to satisfy a checker. The method belongs on EventBus next to publishRaw()/ensureConsumerGroup().

qaTrace.q: Does the finding still hold on current origin/master? Two merges landed in the last hour, one of which touched this exact file.
qaTrace.a: Verified by diff: 8232801d1 (#4460/#4481, the GLM-red-forward-fix work) touched collect-state.sh but only added new orch_prs_glm_red / orch_glm_red_forward_fix collectors elsewhere in the file (around line 830+) and did not touch collect_slot_events (line 3032) at all. Read the current function body directly (lines 3032-3075): it is unchanged — still docker exec hydra-redis-1 redis-cli XREAD piped through the ~30-line hand-rolled Python regex parser (re.match(r'^\d+-\d+$', ...)) the issue describes. The worktree's HEAD equals origin/master exactly (8232801d1), so this is not a stale diff. Premise holds; proceeding with a design rather than closing as moot.

qaTrace.q: Is there already a typed consumer-side read of this exact stream we could reuse verbatim?
qaTrace.a: No. src/autopilot/slot-events-bridge.ts reads the stream via eventBus.consume() under a dedicated 'now-pixel-bridge' consumer group and re-broadcasts over WebSocket — a different cursor model (group-tracked, not caller-supplied last-id) and a different transport (WS, not a one-shot HTTP GET a bash collector can curl). cascade-telemetry.ts / candidate-exclusions.ts's fromEvent() helpers parse an already-structured `fields` object (produced by ioredis's native XREADGROUP reply, not by the bridge doing any text parsing) into typed records — they are the RIGHT shape to reuse for field interpretation, but they don't perform the raw stream read themselves, and this concept doesn't need field-level typing at all (the caller, decide.py, wants the raw id/fields envelope, unopinionated about payload shape).

qaTrace.q: Why an EventBus method rather than exposing ioredis's xread() call directly from the new API route?
qaTrace.a: ADR-0017 Category B is explicit: 'the Event Bus owns stream ops; clients use its interface, never the raw connection' and lists exactly this kind of gap-closing (ensureConsumerGroup, publishRaw) as the sanctioned shape. A route handler calling getRedisConnection().xread() directly would be a fresh raw-connection user outside the two sanctioned owners (src/redis/*, event-bus.ts) that decision 5's seam-check extension is designed to catch. Adding the read method next to publishRaw()/ensureConsumerGroup() keeps the raw connection inside the one Module ADR-0017 already designated.

qaTrace.q: Does the three smaller raw-redis-cli reads (collect_redis_queues, collect_scout, collect_arch_cleanup_boards) get folded into this same fix, per the issue's 'Solution' section?
qaTrace.a: No — the issue itself says explicitly to fix collect_slot_events first and treat the other three as optional/acceptable-as-is ('the stream-parsing one is the one with real duplicated logic and real fragility, and is worth fixing first'). This design concept scopes to collect_slot_events only; the three single/double-key reads are out of scope here and would need their own premise check if picked up later.

qaTrace.q: What is the concrete new endpoint shape, and does it fit the existing `collect_orch_board` / `hydra raw GET` pattern the issue points to as the correct precedent?
qaTrace.a: GET /api/autopilot/slot-events?last_id=<id>&count=<n>, mirroring GET /autopilot/board-state (mounted from a new src/api/autopilot-slot-events.ts sub-router alongside the existing autopilot-board.ts / autopilot-control.ts / autopilot-idle.ts / autopilot-lifecycle.ts / autopilot-log.ts / autopilot-runs.ts siblings in src/api.ts, per the documented 'API routes in sub-routers' convention). The handler defaults last_id to '0' and count to 100 (matching HYDRA_AUTOPILOT_SLOT_EVENTS_LAST_ID / HYDRA_AUTOPILOT_SLOT_EVENTS_COUNT's current bash defaults), calls the new EventBus.readRaw(stream, lastId, count) method, and returns {events: [{id, fields}], last_id} as JSON with a 200 even on a Redis-read failure (empty events, null last_id) — same best-effort contract collect_slot_events already promises. collect_slot_events becomes: `hydra raw GET "/autopilot/slot-events?last_id=$SLOT_EVENTS_LAST_ID&count=$SLOT_EVENTS_COUNT"` piped straight into `slot_events_json=`, no python3/regex stage at all.

qaTrace.q: Do the existing HYDRA_AUTOPILOT_SLOT_EVENTS_STREAM / _LAST_ID / _COUNT env-var overrides (used by tests and any operator tooling) still work after routing through HTTP?
qaTrace.a: STREAM stays bash-side only — it already defaults to the single production stream name and nothing overrides it in practice outside tests of collect-state.sh itself; the new endpoint hard-codes the one production stream name (hydra:autopilot:slot-events) rather than accepting a stream-name query param, since accepting an arbitrary stream name over HTTP would turn a narrow autopilot-internal read into a general Redis-stream proxy — an unwanted surface widening. _LAST_ID and _COUNT keep working because they are forwarded as the last_id/count query params collect_slot_events already builds from those same env vars today; only the transport (docker exec redis-cli -> curl) changes, not the override contract.
